extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians, graduate students, and informed readers interested in number theory, automorphic forms, and representation theory
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic overview of the Langlands program: its core conjectures (reciprocity, functoriality, geometric variants), the types of mathematical objects involved, important special cases and known results, and modern geometric reformulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objects for which Langlands conjectures can be stated
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists the mathematical objects/categories across which Langlands conjectures are formulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: representations of reductive groups over local fields (with subcases archimedean, p-adic, completions of function fields); automorphic forms on reductive groups over global fields (subcases number fields or function fields); analogues for finite fields; and more general fields such as function fields over the complex numbers. The page notes that different fields give different versions of the conjectures and that some versions depend on notions (Langlands groups, L-groups) whose definitions or existence are not fixed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocity conjecture
rubrics_metrics.description: Langlands' reciprocity conjecture generalizes Artin reciprocity by relating Artin L-functions of Galois representations to automorphic L-functions coming from automorphic cuspidal representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as giving a correspondence between automorphic representations of a reductive group and homomorphisms from a Langlands group to an L-group; over local fields it parameterizes L-packets of admissible irreducible representations, and over global fields it should parameterize automorphic forms. Historical context: extends Artin's reciprocity (abelian case) and Hecke's relations between Dirichlet L-functions and automorphic forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functoriality conjecture
rubrics_metrics.description: A predicted compatibility: a suitable homomorphism of L-groups should induce a correspondence between automorphic forms (global) or representations (local) of the associated reductive groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functoriality is presented as a general principle that implies many other conjectures; in classical language it generalizes 'liftings' and behaves like an induced-representation construction (covariant). Concrete constructions are known in special cases but a general direct construction remains elusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalized functoriality
rubrics_metrics.description: Langlands' broader formulation replacing GL(n) with arbitrary connected reductive groups and using the Langlands dual group L G to define L-functions for automorphic cuspidal representations of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One conjecture states these L-functions satisfy functional equations generalizing known ones; the Functoriality Principle relates automorphic representations across groups via morphisms of their L-groups and is expected to imply other Langlands conjectures. The description emphasizes the role of finite-dimensional representations of the dual group in constructing L-functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric Langlands conjectures
rubrics_metrics.description: A geometric reformulation of the Langlands program that relates l-adic representations of the étale fundamental group of an algebraic curve to objects in derived categories of l-adic sheaves on the moduli stack of vector bundles on the curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The geometric program attempts to relate more than just irreducible representations; it uses tools from algebraic geometry and category theory (Hecke eigensheaves, derived categories). The page notes recent (2024) progress: a multi-author proof of the categorical, unramified geometric Langlands conjecture is reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Langlands conjectures
rubrics_metrics.description: Conjectures describing a correspondence/parameterization between admissible irreducible representations of reductive groups over local fields and appropriate Galois/Langlands parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists known results and proofs for GL(n) in many cases (archimedean fields by Langlands, p-adic and positive-characteristic local fields by various authors, later proofs by Harris–Taylor, Henniart, Scholze, etc.). It also mentions that over the reals this correspondence is Langlands classification of representations of real reductive groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fargues–Scholze program (geometric recasting of local Langlands)
rubrics_metrics.description: A geometric approach to the local Langlands correspondence using the Fargues–Fontaine curve and the stack Bun_G of G-bundles as a geometric replacement for representation theory over non-archimedean local fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They develop ℓ-adic sheaves on Bun_G, prove a version of geometric Satake for the Fargues–Fontaine curve, define a geometric moduli stack of Langlands parameters, and formulate a conjectural categorical form of local Langlands where correspondences arise from relationships between categories of sheaves and coherent sheaves on the parameter stack. This is a reformulation that yields new results but is not a complete proof for all groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental lemma
rubrics_metrics.description: A key technical identity/conjecture (originally formulated by Langlands and Shelstad) required in proofs of essential conjectures within the Langlands program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page highlights Ngô Bảo Châu's 2008 proof of the fundamental lemma and notes its central role in many arguments toward establishing Langlands-type correspondences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status and known special cases/results
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements of which cases of Langlands conjectures are proved or substantially advanced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: correspondence for GL(1) from class field theory; Langlands' proofs for archimedean local fields (R, C); Lusztig's classification over finite fields as an analogue; Andrew Wiles' modularity theorem as an instance of Langlands reciprocity for certain elliptic curves; Laurent Lafforgue's theorem for GL(n) over function fields; Vincent Lafforgue's half of global correspondence for reductive groups over global function fields; multiple proofs of local Langlands for GL(n) by various authors. These examples serve as benchmarks and milestones for progress in the program.
